translations.text: As we offer you, O Lord, the sacrificial victim of humanity’s reconciliation, we humbly beseech you that your Son himself may bestow the gifts of unity and peace upon all nations. Who lives and reigns for ages of ages.

translations.text: O God, whose Son today ascended into heaven while the Apostles stood by, grant us, we ask, that in accordance with his promise he may live with us always on earth and we may be worthy to live with him in heaven. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for all ages of ages.

after.incipit: Praesta, quaesumus, Domine, ut, secundum promissionem
after.ancient_witness: Ambrosian Missal, Milan1712, In die sancto Pentecostes, printed pp[202, 203]
after.ancient_reading: Praesta, quaesumus, Domine: ut, secundum promissionem Filij tui, Domini nostri, Iesu Christi, Spiritus Sanctus & huius nobis sacrificij copiosius reuelet arcanum, & omnem propitius reseret veritatem. Per eundem Dominum nostrum &c. in vnitate eiusdem Spiritus Sancti.
after.divergence: Local transcription typography: printed long-s normalized to s; physical word divisions joined; source & remains in source body but is compared as et. Explicit source ligature declaration: printed æ/Æ expands to ae/Ae, including Praesta and quaesumus; no frozen source bytes change. Source Filij/sacrificij/reuelet/vnitate correspond to Filii/sacrificii/revelet/unitate under explicitly local i/j and u/v spelling. Secondary omits the four-word apposition Domini nostri Iesu Christi after Filii tui; recipient remains the Father and the Son remains explicitly named. Secondary omits et before huius; the following et omnem remains. The old et…et coordination becomes simple conjunction without adding a new proposition. Source long cue Per eundem Dominum nostrum &c. in vnitate eiusdem Spiritus Sancti is not expanded. Secondary uses Per Christum; independently old complete Per Christum Dominum nostrum is selected in this finite study reconstruction. No same-Son/same-Spirit wording is silently transferred.
after.witness_note: Adapted project study English from the complete Pentecost prayer in the Ambrosian Missal (Milan, 1712), printed pp. 202–203 / whole-source pages 240–241, checked in fresh images. The receiving comparison is the secondary digital reproduction labelled 2002, page 266; fidelity to the printed 2002 book and complete authentic 2008 correspondence remain unestablished. Source long-s and æ/Æ are normalized, lines joined, and i/j and u/v correspondences declared locally; & is retained in the historical body and compared as et. Independent review accepts this finite whole-prayer adaptation and English fidelity for source preparation; exact source registration, conclusion binding and runtime presentation remain integration gates. translations.text: Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that, according to the promise of your Son, the Holy Spirit may disclose to us more abundantly the mystery of this sacrifice and graciously open all truth to us. Through Christ our Lord.

whole_expression_findings.affirmative: The complete old prayer already supplies one continuous movement from offering the victim of human reconciliation to asking the Son for unity and peace for all nations. The revised whole shortens its explicit sacrificial identification and relocates the existing Son reference while retaining the same actors, objects, purpose and requested result. The new petition frame is conventional grammatical reframing of that one unit rather than a new substantive prayer or a selection of unrelated old petitions. Considered together with the independently old complete short conclusion, that constrained abridgment supplies a defensible argument that the new contribution lacks independently original authorship. This is not inferred merely from theological similarity or a small word count.
whole_expression_findings.strongest_contrary: Suppressing the explicit present-sacrifice identification and shortening the divine titles changes the emphasis and rhetorical progression. Choosing those omissions and the replacement petition frame can amount to creative editorial recasting even if every central theological idea is old. Copyright’s low originality threshold does not require a new doctrine. The entire revised sequence is not held in an exact old witness, so its source relationship is a substantive variant and the affirmative conclusion remains qualified.

whole_expression_findings.affirmative: One complete old Trinity prayer supplies the invocation, causal means, command, second petition, intensive human object and everlasting-gift destination in their original sequence. The modern whole changes the conventional designation of the offering object and its necessary agreement without composing a new predicate, image, consequence or clause. The independently old service-gifts designation corroborates conventional diction, but the affirmative argument rests on its constrained use within the already complete and unchanged two-petition structure. The full resulting expression can defensibly be assessed as a conventional object substitution and grammatical adjustment rather than independently creative new authorship.
whole_expression_findings.strongest_contrary: Victim-of-this-offering and gifts-of-our-service are not semantically interchangeable labels. Selecting the latter deemphasizes the explicit sacrificial-victim term and introduces a service-centered characterization. Combining that old phrase with a different old prayer, omitting holy and adjusting agreement can constitute editorial selection and adaptation; age of both ingredients is insufficient by itself. No exact independently old whole witness of the revised sequence is established.

whole_expression_findings.affirmative: The complete old prayer already connects Christ’s ascent before the Apostles and his promise with both earthly companionship and our heavenly companionship. The revision changes who is addressed, but consistently preserves who ascended, promised and accompanies us. Its linked verb and pronoun conversions are determined by that single address conversion; it introduces no new action, subject of the ascension or promise, substantive petition, scene or outcome. The remaining changes abridge qualifications and replace the aid phrase with conventional petition framing. Considered as the complete expression, this is defensibly a constrained address conversion and abridgment of one old unit rather than a newly constructed prayer. The separate complete ending is independently old and selected by an actually witnessed receiving cue.
whole_expression_findings.strongest_contrary: Addressing the Father instead of Christ is meaningful theological and rhetorical editing, and suppressing the old majesty, resurrection and aid clauses is deliberate selection. A derivative prayer can acquire original authorship through the combined recasting even without adding a new event. Referential consistency proves fidelity, not copyright status. No exact old whole witness establishes this revised sequence, and the old source alone cannot clear the modern expression.

whole_expression_findings.affirmative: The independently old prayer already contains the entire Son-promise/Holy-Spirit/sacrificial-mystery/all-truth structure, in the same order and with the same Father as addressee. Removing the conventional explicit Son apposition leaves the same already named referent; simplifying et...et to the surviving conjunction introduces no new relation or selected petition. The separate standard short conclusion changes the expression and is disclosed, but is independently old in its complete words. Taken as this finite whole, these are defensible nonoriginal changes; no creative new petition architecture or changed divine agent is supplied. Accepted under policy1 item6/8.2 as a qualified nonoriginal study adaptation, not exact historical identity.
whole_expression_findings.strongest_contrary: The shortened Christ-title apposition, conjunction and conclusion are actual editorial changes. Protected derivative expression can use entirely old words; showing every fragment somewhere is insufficient. This is why the acceptance depends on the preserved whole prayer and its same addressee/referents/coordination, plus an exact independently witnessed formula, rather than a word-count threshold or mechanical cue expansion.
